data.answer: Restores are tested every quarter. The most recent restore test was on 12 September 2026 and was completed in 2 hours 40 minutes, within the 4-hour RTO.

Nimbus Labs uses 9 sub-processors that may process customer data. Customers receive 30 days' advance notice before a new sub-processor is added, and the current list is shared with customers on request.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed once a year, and Tier 2 vendors are reviewed every two years. Any vendor that suffers a security incident is reviewed immediately.
Yes, a background check covering identity, employment history, and education is completed before the start date for every employee, intern, and contractor.
All access is revoked within 4 hours of the person's exit time.
No, while customer data is stored in India by default (AWS Mumbai), disaster recovery copies are held in Singapore.

The provided knowledge chunks only detail notification commitments when a breach involving customer data is confirmed (within 72 hours) and for reportable cyber incidents to CERT-In (within 6 hours). They do not mention a notification commitment specifically for suspected, not yet confirmed, security incidents.

The provided knowledge chunks do not mention encryption of data while it is in use (such as confidential computing); they only cover encryption at rest and field-level encryption for sensitive fields.

The provided chunks outline incident response severity levels and acknowledgment times (e.g., P1 within 15 minutes, P2 within 1 hour, P3 within 1 business day, P4 within 3 business days) as well as recovery objectives (RPO of 1 hour, RTO of 4 hours), but do not explicitly state general contractual support hours.
The provided knowledge chunks do not contain information regarding whether personal (BYOD) devices can be used to access customer data.
